[[File:Swblasterrack.jpg|thumb|300px|A blaster rack onboard the first Death Star]]
'''Blaster racks''' were small, wall mounted holsters meant to hold [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] and other weapons for easy access. They were commonly used by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].

==Description==
Several different models of blaster racks existed. One such model consisted of several holsters that attached to a slanted portion of a wall, with a long bar on the floor, meant to vertically hold a weapon in place at an angle, with its base touching the floor.<ref name="SWCCG">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Blaster Rack}}</ref> Another model consisted of simple hooks on a wall that a weapon could be placed onto, also vertically, though without the slanted angle and lifted entirely off the ground.<ref name="Episode VI">{{Film|VI}}</ref> Both models could hold various armament, such as [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifles]] and [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonators]].<ref name="SWCCG" />

==History==
[[File:NAVYTRP.png|thumb|left|200px|A blaster rack in the back of the second Death Star's command center]]
Blaster racks were commonly used by the Galactic Empire within various Imperial facilities, such as the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Stars]] and [[Garrison/Legends|garrison]] bases. They were placed in key locations in order to equip [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] with weapons if necessary. On the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]], [[Docking Bay 327/Legends|Docking Bay 327's]] [[Docking Control Room 327|control room]] contained a slanted blaster rack, capable of holding four weapons.<ref name="SWCCG" /> It was destroyed during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] when the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] managed to make the battlestation explode in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].<ref name="Episode IV">{{Film|IV}}</ref>

The station's successor, the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]], also contained a blaster rack, located in its [[Death Star command center|command center]], though this rack was of the non-slanted model and was able to hold at least two blasters. It held two [[A280 blaster rifle/Legends|A280 blaster rifles]] and was destroyed as well, when the second Death Star exploded at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].<ref name="Episode VI" />
